decisions.reason: As a close-to-core app launched as a publicly announced 'new product line' on its own page, it carries visible commitment and likely development investment, which makes management inclined to persist with it.

The education institute extends the firm's training and practitioner-support capabilities, so despite more modest public commitment than a flagship software launch, management has reasons to keep backing it.
A remote support tool fits tightly with the firm's installed base and service model, and that operational complementarity makes it worth retaining even if it was presented less prominently.
The analytics dashboard was given its own page and matches the firm's stated direction toward more digital and efficiently managed practices, so escalation of commitment points to continuation.
A complete practice bundle is very close to the core business, strategically central, and visibly marketed on its own page, making it the kind of offer management is least likely to withdraw.

The job and practice listing portal is distant from the established offer and appears to have received only limited public commitment, so it is the easiest product to discontinue when resources are reviewed.
